sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU investment protection treaties administered via the Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Law), implementing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 March 2019 on its practical modalities; Law of 10 July 2020 amending the RBE regime; Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 on information accompanying funds transfers; CSSF Regulation 12-02 and CSSF AML/CFT circulars; Criminal Code Article 506-1 et seq.; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, Articles 903-1 to 903-9 (SCSp legal framework).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / certificate of existence of each corporate UBO or general partner entity (extrait du RCS or foreign equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) or competent company registrar in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Biometric passport copy and proof of residential address for each individual UBO and general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority / utility provider or credit institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague signatory states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and AML/KYC clearance issued by the intended Luxembourg credit institution or PSF
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg bank or professional of the financial sector (PSF)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original sealed issuer attestation (no apostille required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft notarial or private-writing partnership agreement (convention de société) of the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille solely where executed in notarial authentic form

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of clean criminal record (casier judiciaire) for the general partner and appointed manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Ministry of Justice or competent authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the Luxembourg MAEE or foreign competent authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based PEP identification and enhanced due diligence under Article 5 of the AML/CFT Law, covering PEPs, family members and close associates, with board-level approval for PEP acceptance; continuous screening of all UBOs, the general partner, charterers and counterparties against the Luxembourg national asset-freezing list, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN List for USD clearing transactions, and FATF high-risk jurisdiction lists, supported by adverse-media and negative-news alerting.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online pre-check portal at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be registered in any language using Latin script, with French and German accepted as statutory languages; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin characters for RCS indexing; the name of an SCSp must include the mandatory designation 'Société en commandite spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp' and must be distinctive, non-misleading and not contrary to public order.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 days of a formal RCS refusal, the applicant may file a recours gracieux (friendly reconsideration) with the RCS registrar, attaching amended name variants and legal argument; if refused or left unanswered, a recours en annulation must be lodged with the Tribunal administratif within 3 months of notification, through a Luxembourg-bar avocat, on grounds of excess of power, violation of the law or failure to provide reasons; a favourable final judgment obliges the RCS to re-examine the name application within 48 hours.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A domiciliation or virtual correspondence address in Luxembourg is acceptable for RCS registration, but only if the SCSp can evidence central administration actually exercised in Luxembourg; for an ISIC 5012 deep-sea RoRo shipping SCSp, a pure mail-forwarding address without local management, substance and decision-making records will not support Luxembourg tax residence and may be disregarded for ATAD, CFC and substance-analogue purposes; vessel management and charter operations should be delegated to a resident ship-management company.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-low: estimated 20–25% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within a 36-month operational cycle by the RBE controller, the FIU (Cellule de Renseignements Financiers) or the Luxembourg tax administration (AED), rising above 40% where the general partner is non-EU managed, no Luxembourg bank account is maintained, or the RoRo fleet is chartered exclusively to a non-arm's-length affiliate; mitigation measures include a physical registered office, resident managers, in-person statutory meetings in Luxembourg and full books and records retention in the Grand Duchy.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee for electronic filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory MAEE apostille fees, notarial certification fees at EUR 60–80 per document and sworn translation tariffs of EUR 35–60 per page; bundle estimate approximately EUR 600

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark EUR 3,500–6,500 depending on UBO chain depth, general partner jurisdiction and RoRo charter review

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed screening data provider or CSSF-regulated PSF
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 250–400 per screened party per annum, multi-party bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and professional domiciliation services, first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 1,200–1,800 per annum under CSSF rules on professional domiciliation and AML duties

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: certificate of good standing EUR 100–300; ship ownership and mortgage search EUR 150–250

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 101 to 103 regarding the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp), as introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés de Luxembourg (RCSL), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via the online portal www.lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (signed SCSp partnership agreement), filed electronically with the RCSL and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an SCSp; partners freely determine capital contributions in cash or in kind; no escrow bank account requirement under Luxembourg law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the Partnership Agreement of Société en Commandite Spéciale ('SCSp') is hereby approved, and the initial partnership interests subscribed by the General Partner and the initial Limited Partner are accepted and recorded in the capital table; (2) the registered office of the SCSp is fixed at [Registered Office Address], Luxembourg; (3) [Name] is appointed as Manager (Gérant) with full powers to act as Chief Executive and to represent the SCSp; (4) the Managers are authorised to open bank accounts, execute the filing of the constitutive deed with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL), effect publication in the RESA, and initiate all tax, VAT, and maritime licensing registrations; (5) any Manager acting alone may sign all ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR / RCSL) online portal, www.lbr.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name availability request for '[Proposed Name] SCSp' through the LBR search interface; reserve the approved corporate name to prevent third-party filing during the incorporation dossier preparation.
required_dossiers: List of up to five proposed names
Passport copy of the general partner's ultimate beneficial owner
Certificate of existence of any corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or conflicts with an existing registered mark, promptly resubmit with an alternative name variant; the refusal decision may be appealed to the RCSL registrar within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the SCSp Constitutive Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCSL; a Luxembourg notary is optional unless real property is contributed in kind.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the acte constitutif setting out the corporate name, registered office address in Luxembourg, corporate purpose (deep-sea Ro-Ro vehicle transport), financial year, capital contribution schedule, rights of general and limited partners, and powers of the Gérant. Execute the deed by all partners; signatures may be private unless notarization is requested.
required_dossiers: Capital subscription forms signed by each partner
Resolutions of any corporate partner approving the SCSp constitution

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct corporate, municipal and net wealth taxation; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT, registration duties and indirect taxes; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) for entity registration. Digital access through MyGuichet.lu and the official tax e-services portals.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SCSp, foreign founders must first register the entity with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) to obtain the national business identification number (matricule). Thereafter, before commencing taxable supplies, VAT registration must be filed with the AEDT through MyGuichet.lu; direct tax registration with the ACD is only required at the level of the partners because the SCSp is fiscally transparent. The statutory tax number is the matricule; the VAT identification number is the national number prefixed by 'LU' (e.g., LU + eight digits). Non-resident partners or managers acting through a Luxembourg fixed establishment use the same procedure; where no fixed establishment exists, a Luxembourg fiscal representative may be required for VAT purposes. Registration should be completed within 15 days of the event triggering taxability.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible (fiscally transparent by default under Luxembourg law; not Entity_Level_Taxation, not Territorial_Scope, not Tax_Exempt_Zone; profits and capital are attributed directly to partners for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under Article 168bis LIR, an SCSp may irrevocably elect to be treated as a Luxembourg capital company subject to corporate income tax, thus abandoning fiscal transparency. Luxembourg does not apply a US-style check-the-box election; however, the transparent status may be confirmed through domestic-law characterisation rules and applicable double tax treaties. Hybrid mismatch elections and notifications apply under Luxembourg's implementation of ATAD II, requiring taxpayers to assess and report potential hybrid deductible/financial instrument mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA) under the amended Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for Luxembourg-established small businesses claiming the small-business exemption; EUR 10,000 intra-EU distance-selling threshold under the OSS regime for sales to Luxembourg consumers; no general threshold for non-established entities making taxable B2B supplies in Luxembourg, for import VAT, or for reverse-charge supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently impose a real-time transaction clearance or continuous transaction control (CTC) regime for B2B sales; no government API or digital stamping is required. Paper or XML e-invoices are valid if they preserve authenticity and integrity, and B2G invoices are exchanged through the national PEPPOL infrastructure. All invoices must be retained for 10 years in line with Luxembourg tax record-keeping rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to exports of vehicles from Luxembourg to non-EU destinations when the goods are physically removed from the EU within the statutory time limit (generally 90 days), evidenced by a valid customs export declaration, and when the exporter receives consideration from a non-Luxembourg customer. International deep-sea RoRo transport and directly linked ancillary services (stevedoring, handling, freight forwarding) are VAT-exempt with deduction of input VAT when they serve the direct needs of goods departing to or arriving from a non-EU place. B2B place-of-supply rules determine whether the service is taxable in Luxembourg.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / NCTS electronic clearance record)
Original maritime Bill of Lading (full set duly endorsed)
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of freight payment in foreign currency from the non-EU customer
Proof of discharge and destination (port delivery order or destination-country customs import documentation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and Luxembourg customs scrutinise export zero-rating claims through documentary audits. Failure to substantiate physical export within the prescribed deadline or submission of false evidence triggers retrospective reversal of the zero-rating, assessment of Luxembourg VAT at 17% on freight and ancillary charges, denial of input VAT recovery, statutory late-payment interest, and penalties ranging from 10% to 100% of the tax evaded depending on good faith. Deliberate fraudulent export-zero-rating claims may lead to criminal fines and imprisonment, and tax audits may be reopened within the general assessment periods extended to 10 years for fraud; customs post-clearance recovery applies under the EU Customs Code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting under the European Central Bank (ECB) framework, with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the competent banking licensing and prudential supervision authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg provides full current and capital account convertibility under EU law and the euro-area legal framework. There are no exchange-control approvals, no investment permits, and no profit repatriation restrictions for non-resident general or limited partners of an SCSp. Practical hurdles arise mainly from bank KYC and substance requirements: distributions to partners must be supported by genuine economic activity, transfer pricing documentation, and intercompany agreements to avoid recharacterisation under the Luxembourg GAAR, DAC6 or ATAD rules. Payments above EUR 12,500, or equivalent in foreign currency, between a resident bank and a non-resident are reported to the BCL on a monthly basis for balance-of-payments statistics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio in Luxembourg. Freight income and vessel charter-hire collections from Ro-Ro ocean carriage may be retained in EUR, USD, or any other currency selected for the treasury operation. However, all export-related inward remittances received on a Luxembourg-resident account must be identifiable for BCL balance-of-payments reporting and, for practical bank screening, should include a commercial invoice, bill of lading, or charter party reference.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse de l'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Multi-Currency Account / Export Credit Facilities
Operational Account / Commodity and Trade Finance Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium – subject to material limitation. Luxembourg-authorised Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions can be used as a supplementary treasury clearing track for low-value operational expenses and euro liquidity pooling, but they cannot replace a credit institution for the core cross-border trade finance function. Offshore digital EMIs, unless they hold a Luxembourg/CSSF licence or a valid EU passport with an agent bank in Luxembourg, are not viable for the SCSp because they generally cannot open high-value corporate accounts, issue Commercial Letters of Credit, or offer SWIFT MT103/MT202 clearing with proper BCL reporting. Such accounts should be restricted to non-core, low-transaction-value ancillary services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed SCSp controlled by non-resident partners, physical presence is generally required for at least one authorised signatory and the ultimate beneficial owner at the account-opening interview in Luxembourg. Some banks allow a partial remote onboarding mechanism with a certified video interview and notarised KYC documents, but this is discretionary and rarely granted without an existing bank relationship. The General Partner's managing director or a person with equivalent senior authority must attend the interview, present the original passport, and confirm the partnership's intended commercial substance and payment rails.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp is not yet fully transparent in the Luxembourg RBE register, or the beneficial owner chain wraps multiple non-EEA jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership agreement and private placement or capital call documents; RBE register filing confirmation or exemption certificate; fully documented UBO ownership chart; notarised ID/passport copies; proof of registered office; opening bank reference from the general partner's home bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital inflow originates from non-EEA partner jurisdictions, creating source-of-funds scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements and bank statements of contributing partners; signed source-of-wealth declaration; commercial documentation proving the partner's lawful operating profit; preliminary capital call notice; KYC questionnaire with explanation of the shipping business model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Vessel trading or port call patterns conflict with EU restrictive measures, including Russia, Iran, Syria, or North Korea related cargoes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Charter party containing sanctions-compliant warranties; latest denial-of-service and restrictive trade clauses; fleet IMO number flags; vessel P&I Club confirmation; automated sanctions screening log; port-call schedule certified by the commercial or port agent; cargo manifest evidence for non-sanctioned vehicles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through partnership with no minimum capital is assessed as a potential 'empty shell' or unregulated fund vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence of active Ro-Ro commercial operations: bareboat or time charter agreements, freight invoices, bill-of-lading repository, port receipts, bunker supply contracts, employee social security registrations, office lease, and a forward-looking cash-flow model demonstrating emergency working capital.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant capital subscription is executed through SWIFT MT103 from the partner's account to the Luxembourg SCSp's IBAN account, with a clear purpose declaration such as 'capital contribution to Luxembourg SCSp'. The originator must provide the full legal name, address, account number (IBAN for EEA banks or valid account/Fedwire routing for third countries), and the relevant BCL balance-of-payments item code for direct investment. Any remittance exceeding EUR 12,500 is automatically captured by the receiving bank in the BCL statistical report; the SCSp must therefore attach a capital call notice signed by the General Partner and, where applicable, the contribution allocation schedule to allow the bank to classify the entry accurately.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade payments for port disbursements, stevedoring, tug services, brokers, charter hire and vessel repairs are cleared via SWIFT MT103 wires denominated in EUR, USD or GBP as suited to the counterparty. Large one-time vessel acquisition or charter-delivery payments use SWIFT MT202/MT202COV. Where required by the commercial contract, the SCSp can open or receive a Commercial Letter of Credit through SWIFT MT700, with the nominated bank acting as issuing, advising or confirming bank, ensuring that underlying shipping documents and invoices are consistent with UCP 600. All outbound wires must carry the beneficiary bank identifier (IBAN, Fedwire or CHIPS routing) and the SCSp's counterparty reference for merchantable AML and sanctions screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Option (vanilla call/put and collar structures)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of Ultimate Beneficial Owners in the Luxembourg RBE register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) via Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days of the RBE registration anniversary; also within 30 days of any UBO or shareholding change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines EUR 250–EUR 1,250 for late or missing confirmation; EUR 2,500–EUR 25,000 for deliberate false declarations with possible imprisonment up to 6 months; sanctions published and RBE non-compliance flag set

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit for the SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers e-filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of financial year-end (partner approval within 6 months, deposit within 1 month thereafter); 31 July for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal default notice and public non-compliance notation; court-ordered coercive fine (astreinte) up to EUR 500 per day of delay; criminal fine up to EUR 1,250; persistent non-filing for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the SCSp exceeds at least two of the three Luxembourg GAAP size tests on two consecutive balance sheet dates: total assets EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average workforce 50 FTE. Small SCSp remain exempt but must still file abridged annual accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 (plan comptable normalisé); IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for non-listed undertakings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must file its initial UBO declaration and thereafter confirm it annually within 30 days of the RBE registration anniversary; every transfer of partnership interests must be declared within 30 days and also recorded in the register of partners and minutes of partner decisions. Beneficial ownership is assessed on individuals ultimately owning or controlling more than 25% of the partnership. Public access to the RBE remains restricted following the CJEU ruling in C-37/20, but filing and annual confirmation duties are unchanged.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Partner and Manager Decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,500–USD 6,500 per annum (Luxembourg fiduciary/PFS market range for registered office, corporate secretarial support, and RCS/RBE e-filing handling)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500–USD 10,900 per annum (EUR 5,000–EUR 10,000) for a standard SCSp RoRo shipping entity audit; fee increases with group consolidation and complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% corporate income tax (IRC), reduced to 15% on the first EUR 175,000 of taxable income; plus 7% solidarity surcharge; plus municipal business tax of 6.75% for Luxembourg City, giving an aggregate headline effective rate of 24.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp default is pass-through taxation with profits taxed at partner level. Eligible shipping operators may elect Luxembourg's optional tonnage tax regime, replacing normal CIT on RoRo shipping profits with a notional profit calculated by net tonnage. Partial exemptions apply for qualifying IP income (up to 80%), and participation-exempt dividends are tax exempt.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 470 (SCSp annual information and partnership tax return) filed through the Luxembourg Administration des contributions directes e-file portal (MyGuichet.lu secure e-space).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return due on 31 December of the year following the accounting year-end. An extension to 30 June of the second subsequent year is available when the return is prepared by an approved tax adviser and filed electronically.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp name, RCS/BRN number, registered office, legal form, tax office, fiscal year, and type of partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Luxembourg RCS number and registered office of the SCSp. Non-resident partner names are not generally listed on the local return, but relevant foreign address information must be attached for allocation purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net result according to the accounts, including RoRo charter hire, voyage revenue, vessel operating expenses, crew costs, insurance, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only that portion of profit attributable to the Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) when the SCSp carries on trade through a Luxembourg PE. Income exempt under a tax treaty or without a PE may be excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Non-deductible expenses and adjustment add-backs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back non-deductible provisions, disguised profit distributions, 50% of certain entertainment costs, excessive management fees, and transfer pricing adjustments under Article 56bis LIR.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must apply the same add-backs to the Luxembourg PE profit computation and keep evidence that the costs are arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare participation-exempt dividends, capital gains, tonnage-tax notional profit if elected, and other statutory deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty benefits for non-resident partners are assessed separately at partner level. The SCSp return should not claim treaty exemptions on behalf of non-residents unless a corresponding PE disclosure is made.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State total available tax losses brought forward and utilized in the current period, with a note on the 17-year carry-forward limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss utilization is computed at the partner level for transparent SCSp entities; non-resident partners may claim losses only to the extent attributable to a Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership profit or loss allocation to each partner according to the SCSp partnership deed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the exact allocation percentages, residence addresses and tax identification numbers of non-resident partners, to permit the Luxembourg tax administration to issue partner assessment notices.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing may trigger an ex-officio assessment and a surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax, plus default interest of 0.6% per month. Failure to provide partnership allocation information can attract administrative fines up to EUR 25,000; fraudulent omission may lead to criminal prosecution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 470-CIT (if the SCSp has exercised the option for corporate taxation or is required to file a corporate income tax return at entity level) filed via the ACD e-file portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on 31 December following the fiscal year end; electronically assisted returns prepared by a certified tax adviser may be extended to 30 June of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity name, SCSp legal form, RCS number, registered office, fiscal year, and accounting standards applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner that has made the transparency/opacity election must identify itself on a separate non-resident return and reference the Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit per audited financial statements, including international RoRo transport income, vessel hire, and ancillary logistics revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the income attributable to the Luxembourg PE is subject to Luxembourg CIT; treaty shipping article must be invoked where no PE exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report arm's length adjustments to related-party charter rates, vessel management charges and intercompany services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident counterparties must support their pricing with a benchmark and file Luxembourg TP documentation if required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 10 - Taxable result and loss carry-forward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable income after add-backs, exemptions, tonnage-tax application, and deductible prior-year losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, include only the proportion sourced to the Luxembourg PE and attach a detailed allocation statement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or missing corporate filing results in a surcharge up to 10% of tax, default interest at 0.6% monthly, and potential fines up to EUR 125,000 for intentional fraud. Directors may be assessed personally for tax and penalties where the omission is deliberate.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard withholding tax on Luxembourg-source dividends. The rate is reduced to 0% under the Luxembourg participation exemption or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive when the corporate partner holds at least 10% for an uninterrupted 12-month period. Profit allocations made by a transparent SCSp to partners are generally not treated as dividends and carry no Luxembourg withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced dividend withholding rate under a DTA, the beneficial owner must provide the Luxembourg paying agent with a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) and a completed treaty-relief form, accompanied by an ownership declaration and current holding period evidence. If the distribution was already subject to 15% withholding, the beneficiary may apply to the Luxembourg ACD for a refund of the excess within the statutory time limit; refund claims generally must be accompanied by a TRC and a beneficial ownership statement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid by a Luxembourg entity to non-residents is exempt from statutory withholding tax (except specific debt-linked cases). Royalties paid for IP, trademarks or know-how face 0% statutory Luxembourg withholding tax. Under the EU Interest and Royalty Directive, associated EU companies may also benefit from a 0% rate when holding at least 25% for 24 months or based on a DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg Local File is mandatory when annual intercompany transactions exceed EUR 100,000 per transaction category. A Master File is required when the worldwide group consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 350 million. Country-by-Country Reporting filing threshold is EUR 750 million consolidated group revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain a separate ESR statute in the style of offshore centers, but the substance requirement is enforced through the general anti-abuse rule (Article 6 LIR), Article 56bis LIR on transfer pricing, and administrative doctrine. An SCSp in the deep-sea RoRo trade must demonstrate genuine activity in Luxembourg, including strategic chartering decisions, vessel/voyage management, local staff, offices, and assumption of maritime commercial risk. Failure to show substance can result in denial of treaty benefits, tonnage-tax exclusion, recharacterization, and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately misreporting RoRo charter income, invoicing fictitious voyage costs, suppressing vessel hire revenues, or using dual sets of books to escape Luxembourg corporate tax and municipal business tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty equal to 50% of the evaded tax plus default interest at 0.6% per month; criminal exposure of a fine up to EUR 125,000 and imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years under Article 218-219 LIR.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A manager or general partner who knowingly procures the evasion is jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid taxes and penalties, may have personal bank accounts frozen, and can receive a travel ban pending criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Luxembourg SCSp with no physical office, no full-time staff, no vessel management decision-making, and using back-to-back charter contracts solely to book RoRo profits and claim DTA or tonnage-tax benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the SCSp, reallocation of profits to the true economic owner, denial of treaty and tonnage-tax benefits, a penalty up to 50% of the under-declared CIT, plus interest and recovery of unpaid municipal tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the veil and hold the general partner and de facto directors personally liable for the re-assessed tax, penalties, and restitution of unpaid dividends; injunctions and contempt proceedings may be issued for non-cooperation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register ultimate beneficial owners of the SCSp in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), or accepting high-value RORO freight payments without robust customer due diligence when the SCSp acts as a pass-through vehicle for undisclosed partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 50,000 plus EUR 2,500 per day for continuing non-filing; criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 for laundering proceeds associated with the vessel operation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners are personally liable for civil restitution, can be disqualified from managing Luxembourg companies, and may face imprisonment up to 5 years for culpable money-laundering facilitation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Transfer Pricing / False WHT Certification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating fictitious intercompany benchmark studies, executing offsetting invoices for RoRo vessel charters without operational reality, or submitting a forged tax residence certificate to obtain DTA relief on partnership profit repatriation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment with 50% penalty on the under-declared tax, default interest, administrative fine up to EUR 125,000, and revocation of the treaty relief granted.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director signing false documentation becomes personally liable for the withholding tax and penalties recovered from the group, and may be prosecuted with custodial sentences up to 5 years and asset seizure orders.
